cards.claim: Multigrid training (small→large spatial/temporal sizes) accelerates training without accuracy loss when paired with dynamic learning rate scheduling
cards.conditions: Video super-resolution: BasicVSR-M, BasicVSR, EDVR-M on REDS and Vimeo-90K datasets
cards.evidence: Experimental results on two datasets, multiple model architectures
cards.quote: Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method is capable of largely speeding up training (up to speedup in wall-clock training time) without performance drop for various VSR models.

cards.claim: Dynamic learning rate scheduler (restart at large value on each size switch) is critical for multigrid training; naive multigrid causes accuracy drop
cards.conditions: VSR: BasicVSR, EDVR; varying spatial/temporal sizes during training
cards.effect: Required to prevent accuracy degradation; enables 3–6× speedup vs. baseline
cards.evidence: Ablation implicit in design justification; paper shows speedup only with scheduler
cards.quote: Simply applying the above multigrid strategy to VSR training causes an accuracy drop. The devil is the learning rate scheduler... we propose a dynamic learning rate scheduler, which adjusts the learning rate to fit the different degrees of task difficulty when switching spatial/temporal sizes. Specifically, the scheduler re-starts the learning rate with large values when the spatial or temporal size changes.

cards.claim: Simultaneous spatial and temporal size increases cause sub-optimal results; hierarchical design (spatial cycle containing temporal sub-cycles) is superior
cards.conditions: VSR: spatial and temporal sizes both variable
cards.effect: Prevents accuracy loss vs. simultaneous changes
cards.evidence: Experimental observation; paper justifies design choice
cards.quote: Moreover, our experiments suggest that directly increasing the spatial and temporal sizes at the same time leads to sub-optimal results. Thus, rather than changing them synchronously, we adopt a hierarchical design with two cycles for altering spatial and temporal sizes.

cards.claim: Linear learning rate scaling rule: when minibatch size increases N-fold, scale learning rate by N to maintain training dynamics
cards.conditions: Large minibatch training (BS 16→64); VSR models (BasicVSR-M, EDVR-M)
cards.effect: Maintains convergence; without scaling, 0.3 PSNR drop (30.91→30.64)
cards.evidence: Ablation study (Table 4); validated across multiple VSR models
cards.quote: Similar to [ 13 ] , we apply a linear scaling rule to adjust the learning rate according to minibatch sizes.

cards.claim: Warmup phase (gradual learning rate increase from small value) is necessary for large minibatch training to work
cards.conditions: Large minibatch training (BS 64); VSR: BasicVSR-M on REDS
cards.effect: Without warmup, PSNR drops 0.10 (30.91→30.81); with warmup achieves 30.93
cards.evidence: Ablation study comparing w/o, constant, and linear warmup
cards.quote: In addition, it is necessary to have a warmup phase that trains the network with a small learning rate early in training.

cards.claim: Linear learning rate scaling + warmup together enable large batch (4× increase) without accuracy loss
cards.conditions: VSR: BasicVSR-M on REDS; minibatch 16→64, 300k→75k iterations
cards.quote: directly increasing the minibatch size leads to a performance drop. Whereas, when conducting learning rate scaling, large minibatch training (with warmup) achieves comparable performance to baseline.

cards.claim: Small spatial sizes (<64 px) cause large accuracy drop due to insufficient optical flow information; minimum viable size required
cards.conditions: VSR spatial size selection; recurrent and sliding-window architectures
cards.effect: Very small sizes (e.g., 32 px implied) lead to accuracy degradation
cards.evidence: Design justification for minimum spatial size choice (96 px, 128 px used in experiments)
cards.quote: training with a very small spatial size ( e.g., ) leads to a large accuracy drop. The reason might be the unsatisfying optical flow estimation due to the insufficient information produced by such small patches. Therefore, the spatial sizes in the spatial cycle should not be too small.

cards.claim: Very small temporal sizes (e.g., 1 frame) provide insufficient complementary temporal information; minimum temporal size needed
cards.conditions: VSR temporal size selection; recurrent-based methods (BasicVSR)
cards.effect: Too-small temporal sizes severely degrade performance
cards.evidence: Design justification; temporal range {1,3,5} or {1,5,7} used in practice
cards.quote: the performance of VSR drops a lot with a very small temporal size ( e.g., ), as too few adjacent frames could not provide enough complementary information.
